title: Equivariant projective spreading of a generic normalization
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $Y$ be a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme, and let $g:C\to Y$ be a proper dominant morphism, with $C$ integral of finite type over $k$ and geometrically integral generic fibre of dimension one. Put $K=k(Y)$ and $F=k(C)$. Let a finite group $H$ act compatibly on $k,C,Y,g$. Let $K_0/K$ be a finite purely inseparable extension with an extending $H$-action. Put $F_0=F\otimes_KK_0$, suppose it is a field, and let $N$ be the normalization of $(C\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}K_0)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Assume $N$ is smooth and geometrically integral over $K_0$. Let $D\subset N$ be an $H$-stable finite etale closed subscheme, possibly empty. Let $S_0$ and $C_0$ be the normalizations of $Y$ in $K_0$ and of $C$ in $F_0$, respectively. They are normal integral excellent Noetherian finite-type $k$-schemes with the specified function fields, their maps to $Y,C$ are finite and dominant, and $S_0$ is projective over $k$. There is a canonical proper $H$-equivariant map $C_0\to S_0$ making the square with $g$ commute, and its generic fibre is canonically $N$ over $C$ and $K_0$. The actions on $k,Y,C,K_0,F_0$ extend to $S_0,C_0$. There exists an integral excellent Noetherian finite-type $k$-scheme $T$ with a compatible $H$-action and an equivariant proper birational morphism $q:T\to C_0$, such that $T/k$, $q$, and $T\to S_0$ are H-projective. Its generic fibre over $S_0$ maps isomorphically to $N$. If $L\subset T$ is the schematic closure of $D$ through this isomorphism, then $L$ is $H$-stable, $L_\eta=D$, and all these generic identifications are over $C$ and $K_0$. Birational means an isomorphism between dense open subschemes. Excellence means excellence of affine coordinate rings, and Noetherian means quasi-compact and locally Noetherian.

All group actions are by automorphisms, may be nonfaithful, and commute with the displayed maps; they may act on the ground field. H-projective means admitting a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target, independently of the name of the acting group. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. Schematic closure is the closed subscheme defined by the kernel of restriction of functions to the specified subscheme.

Notions used: [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-pc-field-tower], [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], [def-fin-normalization-extension], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [pqf-def-locnoeth].

source.place: Tag 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), combined with normalization in finite function-field extensions and de Jong (1997), §§2.9–2.10, pp.604–605. Integral closure localization and the generic normal-curve comparison are expanded in the retained parent proof, Steps 5–7.

proof.text: The map $F\to F_0$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, is injective: extend $1\in K_0$ to a $K$-basis. The tensors with this finite basis span $F_0$ over $F$, so $F_0/F$ is finite. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-model-functoriality] to $(Y,K_0)$ and $(C,F_0)$. This gives the specified normal integral finite-type models $S_0,C_0$, their finite surjective maps, their specified function fields, and their compatible semilinear $H$-actions. The field action on $F_0$ is $h(x\otimes a)=h(x)\otimes h(a)$; the tensor relations hold because the two actions agree on $K$. It preserves products and identities and satisfies the group law. Thus the functoriality theorem applies even when $H$ acts on $k$.

Apply [lem-fin-finite-over-projective] to $S_0\to Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its base is affine Noetherian (a field has only the ideals $(0),(1)$), so its final clause gives an actual finite-projective-space embedding of $S_0$ over $k$. In particular $S_0/k$ and $Y/k$ are proper and separated by [lem-pc-projective-proper]. Since $g$ is proper, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a) makes $C/k$ proper. Then [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](c) makes $C_0/k$ proper.

For $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset Y$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset g^{-1}V$, write $A'\subset K_0$ and $B'\subset F_0$ for the integral closures defining the two normalizations [def-fin-normalization-extension]. Every $a\in A'$ satisfies a monic equation over $A$, hence the same equation over $B$; thus $A'\subset B'$. These inclusions define $\operatorname{Spec}B'\to\operatorname{Spec}A'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], the maps restrict to the same inclusions on principal opens; since principal opens form a basis in each affine chart, they glue to $f_0:C_0\to S_0$. The commutative square is exactly the inclusions $A\to A'\to B'$ and $A\to B\to B'$. Applying $h$ to these inclusions gives the corresponding inclusions on the translated charts, so $f_0$ is equivariant. Since $C_0/k$ is proper and $S_0/k$ is separated, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] makes $f_0$ proper.

proof.text: Here is the affine generic-fibre calculation, retaining both structural maps. Fix $A,B,A',B'$ as above and put $S=A\setminus\{0\}$. The ring $S^{-1}A'$ is a domain finite-dimensional over $K$, since $A'/A$ is finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field] it is a field, and its fraction field is $K_0$, so $S^{-1}A'=K_0$. Consequently $B'\otimes_{A'}K_0=S^{-1}B'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], this is the integral closure of $B_K=S^{-1}B$ in $F_0$. The ring $B_K\otimes_KK_0$ embeds into $F\otimes_KK_0=F_0$: tensoring the inclusion $B_K\subset F$ preserves injectivity, as follows by extending a basis of a vector subspace to a basis. It is a domain with fraction field $F_0$, since localizing it at $B_K\setminus\{0\}$ gives the field $F_0$.

source.place: Tag 0307 (lemma-integral-closure-localize); finite-dimensional domain argument of Tag 00GS (lemma-integral-over-field).

proof.text: The ring $B_K\otimes_KK_0$ is finite over $B_K$, with spanning set the tensors of a finite $K$-basis of $K_0$. Therefore it is integral over $B_K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. Their integral closures in $F_0$ coincide: one inclusion follows by keeping a monic equation over $B_K$, and the other follows by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive] applied to the intermediate finite algebra and the algebra generated by an integral element. Thus the ring in Step 4 is exactly the normalization ring of $B_K\otimes_KK_0$. These equalities are equalities of subrings of the specified $F_0$, compatible with localization by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization]. They glue to the canonical isomorphism $(C_0)_{\eta_0}\simeq N$, where $\eta_0=\operatorname{Spec}K_0$ is the generic point of $S_0$. They fix $B$ and $K_0$, hence the isomorphism is over both $C$ and $K_0$ and is equivariant. The reduction in the definition of $N$ changes nothing: the displayed affine generic base-change rings are domains.

The curve $C_\eta\times_KK_0$ has dimension one by [lem-pc-dim-base-change]. It is integral by the affine domain calculation above (all nonempty affine generic charts have the same generic point). Apply [lem-sc-normalization-exists] over the field $K_0$: $N$ is proper, integral, one-dimensional, and has function field $F_0$. Properness of the unnormalized curve follows by base change of $g$ using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). Normality is part of its normalization; smoothness and geometric integrality are the hypotheses of the item.

Apply [lem-sfb-semilinear-equivariant-chow-modification] to the proper integral finite-type $k$-scheme $C_0$ with its action. It gives integral finite-type $T$, the compatible action, and equivariant proper birational $q:T\to C_0$, with both $T/k$ and $q$ H-projective and with the induced identification $k(T)=F_0$. Compose with $f_0$. Since $S_0/k$ is separated, apply [lem-sfb-finite-constant-projective-graph] with the identity finite extension $k/k$, $R=T$, $S=S_0$, and $c=f_0q$. Its closed graph embedding proves that $T\to S_0$ is H-projective in precisely the finite-projective-space convention of the item.

source.place: Tag 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), finite semilinear translates; morphisms.tex Tag 0C4Q (lemma-projective-permanence), closed graph.

proof.text: The generic fibre $T_{\eta_0}$ is integral: each nonempty affine chart above an affine open of $S_0$ is the spectrum of a localization of a domain, by [lem-weil-pbc-generic-fibre-localization-domain-irreducible]. The maps from the base domains are injective since $T\to C_0\to S_0$ induces the inclusion $K_0\subset F_0$. These charts all contain the generic point of $T$; their fraction field remains $F_0$, with its fixed $K_0$-structure [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. The map $q_{\eta_0}:T_{\eta_0}\to N$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b), dominant, and induces the identity on $F_0$. Both source and target are finite type and separated over $K_0$ (the source is H-projective). By [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] applied to each whole underlying space, their dimensions are equal since their generic residue fields are the same $K_0$-field $F_0$. The target has dimension one by Step 6. Hence [lem-trf-proper-birational-normal-curve-iso] applies and makes $q_{\eta_0}$ an isomorphism. It is the isomorphism induced by $q$, so it retains the maps to $C$ and $\operatorname{Spec}K_0$ and the actions.

The schemes $S_0,C_0,T$ are finite type over $k$, so they are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. For excellence, [lem-exc-fields-excellent] gives excellence of $k$, and [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] gives excellence of the finite-type coordinate algebras on a finite affine cover of each scheme. By [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover] all their affine coordinate rings are excellent. This proves exactly the excellence and Noetherian conventions required in the statement, without adding a normality requirement on $T$.

View $D$ inside $T_{\eta_0}$ by the isomorphism of Step 8 and let $j:D\to T$ be the composite. The scheme $D$ is quasi-compact because it is finite over a field. The target $T$ is separated, hence quasi-separated. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $j$ quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel], its scheme-theoretic image $L\subset T$ exists and is defined on every affine open by the kernel of restriction to $D$. This is the schematic closure specified in the item. Every $h$ carries the restriction map to the restriction map on the translated open, because $D$ and its map are invariant. It therefore carries each kernel to the translated kernel. These invariant ideals give the induced $H$-action on $L$, and its group law is inherited by restriction from $T$.

Finally fix an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A'\subset S_0$ and $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset T$ above it, and set $S=A'\setminus\{0\}$. The closed subscheme $D$ of $T_{\eta_0}$ has an ideal $J\subset S^{-1}R$ on this generic affine chart. The kernel defining $L$ is its contraction $I\subset R$. For any $r/s\in J$, $r/1=s(r/s)\in J$, so $r\in I$; conversely $I$ maps into $J$. Thus $S^{-1}I=J$ and $(R/I)\otimes_{A'}K_0=(S^{-1}R)/J$. These identities on affine charts identify $L_{\eta_0}$ with $D$ as closed subschemes under the specified generic isomorphism. If $D$ is empty, $J=S^{-1}R$, $I=R$, and $L$ is empty as well. The calculation fixes $K_0$ and the structural maps to $C$, so all the asserted generic identifications are the specified ones.

The statement is byte-identical to the Q123 parent-split copy; the only stmt_dep added is def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension. There are no new nodes and no repair note, so this is a first split, not a re-split. The item is still unsplit in live and side-live, so it is not superseded. Step checks: (1) F0/F is finite; functoriality gives S0 and C0 with the semilinear action h(x⊗a)=h(x)⊗h(a). (2) Finite-over-projective over Spec k gives S0↪P^N_k; Y is quasi-compact, so it meets the pc-projective convention; C/k and C0/k are proper. (3) A'⊂B' by carrying the monic equation, the affine maps glue, and f0 is proper by proper-to-separated. (4)-(5) S^{-1}A'=K0, S^{-1}B' is the integral closure of B_K in F0 and equals the normalization of B_K⊗_K K0 by integrality and transitivity, so (C0)_{η0}≅N over C and K0. (6) dim 1 and properness of N. (7) The Chow node and the projective-graph node with F=k give T/k, q and T→S0 H-projective, and q is birational because T is integral. (8) T_{η0} is integral of dim trdeg_{K0}F0=1, and the normal-curve-iso node needs only the target normal (checked against Stacks 0BFP). (9) Excellence and Noetherianity via 07QU, 0HAB, 01T6. (10)-(11) The scheme image of the quasi-compact map j gives L, which is H-stable, and the contraction ideal gives L_η=D, nilpotents included; empty D gives empty L. Edge cases Y=Spec k, K0=K, D empty and H nonfaithful or acting on k all work. Stacks tags 0200, 0307, 0BFP, 0AB7, 0HAB, 01R8, 0C4Q, 0BXR, 07QU and 0B3I are present with the stated labels. No SGA is cited.
